messages:
alex.m: quick check — do we want the gateway to hold a per-connection shaping window for streaming requests, or should shaping be pushed entirely to the upstream pool? asking because some customers see long tails when we let upstreams self-regulate.
priya.k: preference: keep short-term shaping at the gateway (10s window) so we can smooth bursts before hitting backend queues. makes retries and hedging cheaper.
samuel: +1. if gateway enforces a shaping window it can also apply an early-abort heuristic when the estimated completion time drifts past client deadline. avoids burning downstream tokens.
jamie: curious about interaction with our retry coordinator — if gateway aborts early, do we count that against the retry budget for the request id? also how do we surface that in traces?
priya.k: proposal: gateway early-aborts are annotated as "shaping-abort" and do NOT consume the request retry quota; they instead increment a shaping-miss metric. actual network timeouts or 5xx from upstream still hit retry budget. keeps semantics clean.
tina: product note — some integrations expect us to always deliver final status even if slow. we need a knob per-route: strict-delivery vs best-effort. default should be best-effort for public APIs.
samuel: agree on per-route override. implementation detail: the gateway should maintain a small per-connection rolling estimator (EWMA) of throughput + an inflight-count ceiling. config example: 
```
shaping:
  window_s: 10
  inflight_limit: 16
  abort_threshold_ms: 1200
  mode: best-effort|strict
```
jamie: how about hedging? if we start hedging at T+200ms, gateway shaping could prevent useless hedges by capping parallel inflight to N. but we must allow explicit hedging for strict routes.
alex.m: good point — need a routing policy that composes: shaping + hedging + fallback. order matters. my vote: shaping -> routing -> hedging -> fallback.
priya.k: agree. also add an operator-visible metric: shaping_reject_rate and shaping_added_latency. helps customers tune.
samuel: one more edge case: partial flushes. if gateway flushes chunks to client while still talking to upstream (proxying), and then decides to early-abort, client may have received an incomplete logical response. do we attach a trailer header indicating "incomplete: true"?
jamie: i think yes — trailers like `x-rw-incomplete: shaping-abort` are useful. for unary requests we return a clear error code instead.
tina: make sure SDKs can surface that to end-users. if we change default behavior, add a 1-month opt-in before flipping for some tenants.
deploy-bot: canary deployed gateway-shaping v2 to us-east-1 (canary=10%). monitoring: shaping_reject_rate=0.3%  latency_p95 +4ms in canary.
alex.m: thanks — if canary metrics look stable by EOD, we'll roll to 50%. anyone object?
samuel: no objections from infra.
priya.k: fine from infra side. i'll open a short RFC with the config knobs and the telemetry contract.
jamie: I'll add tracing flags for shaping-abort and the trailer header to the span schema.
tina: product will prepare a changelog blurb and opt-in plan.
alex.m: perfect. short follow-up: add an explicit test that partial responses include the trailer and that SDKs propagate it.
priya.k: noted, will add tests + gate in CI.
